literal: Knowing moderation, with the one who eats, like pleasure will stand, with the one of excessively great food, disease.
translation: Just as health and pleasure abide with the one who eats with moderation, so does disease dwell with the glutton who overeats excessively.
modern: அளவறிந்து உண்பவனிடத்தில் இன்பம் நிலைத்து நிற்பது போல, மிக அதிகமாக உண்பவனிடத்தில் நோய் நிலைத்து நிற்கும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a striking comparison to emphasize the importance of moderate eating. It states that just as health and happiness (இன்பம்) constantly dwell with a person who understands the proper limit (இழிவு) of their food intake and eats accordingly, disease (நோய்) will permanently reside with the glutton who consumes excessively large amounts of food (கழிபேர் இரையான்). The word 'இழிவு' here refers to the lower or moderate limit of food, indicating eating less than one's full capacity. The poet contrasts 'இன்பம்' (pleasure/health) and 'நோய்' (disease) as constant companions to the moderate eater and the overeater respectively.
